bibliographic.title: A systematic review of ethical considerations of large language models in healthcare and medicine
bibliographic.authors: Muhammad Fareed, Madeeha Fatima, Jamal Uddin, Adeel Ahmed, Muhammad Awais Sattar
bibliographic.citation_apa: Fareed, M., Fatima, M., Uddin, J., Ahmed, A., & Sattar, M. A. (2025). A systematic review of ethical considerations of large language models in healthcare and medicine. Frontiers in Digital Health, 7, 1653631. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2025.1653631

methodology.method_family: systematic review with systematic mapping elements
methodology.study_design: systematic review of peer-reviewed literature using strict eligibility criteria and established guidelines
methodology.sample_description: 27 peer-reviewed studies published between 2017 and 2025 identified across four major open-access databases
methodology.technology_context: large language models (LLMs), ChatGPT, GPT family, transformer architecture, deep learning

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic review of ethical considerations of LLMs in clinical healthcare, directly relevant to governance themes such as accountability, transparency, bias, fairness, privacy, and safety. However, the provided text centers on ethical issues and a provisional ethical integration framework rather than conversational governance, chatbots, guardrails, observability, audit logs, or human oversight in conversational systems. It is best treated as supporting evidence for regulated LLM governance rather than central evidence on conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial introduction were provided; full methods, PRISMA flow, and framework details were not visible. Metadata incorrectly labeled the work as preprint despite journal publication and peer review.

appraisal.notes: Clear review objective and stated use of eligibility criteria, synthesis methods, and guidelines. Sample is modest (n=27) and limited to open-access databases; authors acknowledge the mapping is not exhaustive. Conversational-governance-specific operational controls are not evidenced in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The review appears methodologically structured for its stated ethical-mapping aim, with coherent synthesis of dominant ethical themes in healthcare LLM literature. Relevance to conversational governance is partial because the available text emphasizes bioethical issues and clinical integration rather than conversational system controls.

synthesis.main_claim: Across 27 peer-reviewed studies, bias and fairness are the most frequently discussed ethical concerns for LLMs in healthcare, followed by safety, reliability, transparency, accountability, and privacy, with the GPT family the most examined model group.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a systematic mapping of open-access literature on LLM ethics in healthcare, synthesizes dominant ethical patterns, outlines future research directions, and proposes a provisional ethical integration framework for clinicians, developers, and policymakers.
synthesis.limitations: The synthesis is not exhaustive of all ethical work on LLMs in healthcare, relies on open-access databases, and prior included studies often focus narrowly on specific clinical subdomains.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for ethical and governance-related risk themes in regulated healthcare LLM deployment; not sufficient on its own as central evidence for conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, tracing, contestation, or human handoff.
